simple.meaning: בָּטָא (bâṭâʼ) is a Hebrew action word meaning “to babble ; hence, to vociferate angrily.” BibleIQ anchors the English reading to this source verb before comparing its uses.
simple.biblicalBackground: This action appears 4 times in Leviticus, Psalms, Proverbs, beginning at Leviticus 5:4. Its meaning becomes clearer as the uses are compared.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to בָּטָא (H981) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Actions in Scripture show what people do, what God does, and how covenant faithfulness or rebellion is described. BibleIQ compares the action across its occurrences.
simple.summary: בָּטָא (bâṭâʼ) / H981 is traced through Leviticus 5:4, Psalms 106:33, Proverbs 12:18 with source-language evidence and verse context.

definitions.short: to babble ; hence, to vociferate angrily
definitions.full: H981. bata or batah [ בָּטָא בָּטָה, ] verb speak rashly, thoughtlessly (Late Hebrew id. , בטי ) — Qal Participle בּוֺטֶה Prov 12:18 one that babbleth (opposed to חֲכָמִים לְשׁוֺן ). Pi`el Imperfect בִשְׁבוּעָה יְבַטֵּא Lev 5:4 speak rashly, unadvisedly ; so בִשְׂפָתָיו וַיְבַטֵּא (of Moses) Psa 106:33 ; Infinitive בִשְׂפָתַיִם לְבַטֵּא Lev 5:4 (P).
